Charging more is usually the right move for an early startup. The anchor a buyer uses is
not your cost but the alternative they would otherwise pick, including doing nothing at all.

Raising the price on new customers only is the cheapest experiment available. It costs one
afternoon and it does not disturb the accounts you already have.

A founder who is afraid to raise prices is usually afraid of hearing no. That fear is
information about the founder, not about the market.
